brief.headline: Traffic and users rose sharply, but revenue fell 9.3% to 9,402 as conversion and AOV declined.
executive_summary: Sessions rose 42% to 29,029 and users rose 37.7% to 24,710.
Revenue fell 9.3% to 9,402 while transactions rose 3% to 170.
Conversion rate fell from 0.68 to 0.56 and AOV fell from 62.84 to 55.31.
The previous week included New Year's Eve and New Year's Day, so part of the week-over-week move may be calendar timing.

what_changed.title: Traffic up, revenue down
what_changed.detail: Sessions rose 42% to 29,029, but revenue fell 9.3% to 9,402 and revenue per session fell from 0.51 to 0.32.

what_changed.title: Checkout step weakened
what_changed.detail: Checkout -> purchase fell from 52.87 to 46.96, a -11.2% change, and total conversion rate fell from 0.68 to 0.56.

what_changed.title: US AOV fell sharply
what_changed.detail: United States AOV fell from 79.96 to 47.32, -40.8%, with a -28.8 point gap versus total AOV.

what_changed.title: Mobile revenue recovered
what_changed.detail: Mobile revenue rose 62% to 3,385 and mobile AOV rose from 28.63 to 54.6, a +102.7 point gap versus total AOV.

likely_drivers: The previous week included New Year's Eve and New Year's Day, so the revenue and AOV decline may be calendar timing.
The total traffic_vs_revenue anomaly is consistent with sessions up 42% while revenue fell 9.3%.
The checkout-to-purchase step fell from 52.87 to 46.96, consistent with a checkout-stage issue.
United States AOV fell from 79.96 to 47.32, consistent with lower US order values.
risks: If the checkout-to-purchase decline persists, higher sessions will not convert into revenue.
If US AOV weakness persists, total revenue will remain below the prior week.
If source attribution is not validated, channel decisions may rely on unreliable splits.

actions.action: Audit the final checkout step and run one test on desktop and US sessions.
actions.why: The biggest funnel leak is checkout to purchase, and desktop and US revenue fell while sessions rose.
actions.evidence: Checkout -> purchase: 46.96 vs 52.87, -11.2%; desktop revenue: 5,912 vs 7,948, -25.6%; United States revenue: 3,833 vs 5,437, -29.5%.

actions.action: Validate source, campaign, and channel attribution before reallocating spend.
actions.why: A large share of session source fields is unusable, and channel splits include obfuscated placeholders.
actions.evidence: source unusable_pct: 24.4; session_level_source unusable_pct: 26.5; total sessions: 29,029.

actions.action: Launch a win-back email flow for at-risk high-value customers.
actions.why: At-risk high-value customers increased and have high average spend.
